page: Microsoft Azure D4_v2 is a Dv2-family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features an x86_64 architecture with 8 physical cores and a single thread per core allocation. It is equipped with 28.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB per core, alongside 410 GB of local storage. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression (gzip and bzip3) all scoring in the bottom 10%. Multi-core performance scales to average levels in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, though Geekbench multi-core results remain in the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is average at 551.69 GB/sec for cached blocks, but write bandwidth for large blocks drops to the bottom 25% at 24.46 GB/sec.

Despite the lower-tier single-core compute metrics, the server maintains average performance (middle 50%) for specific workloads including Redis SET operations (8.72 million ops/sec), static web serving (7.77 GB/sec), and database operations. It also handles software compilation and image processing at average tier speeds. Consequently, this instance is suited for legacy multi-threaded applications, basic database hosting, and web serving where high single-thread speed is not a primary constraint. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 410 GB of local storage and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio provides reasonable resource density for general-purpose workloads, though the older CPU architecture represents a performance tradeoff compared to newer generations.
